clue.text: As a hack might be suspended for a grossly exaggerated report of a bloke down under

definitions.text: As a hack might be suspended
definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: a hack is a horse, so this is how a horse would be hanged

definitions.text: grossly exaggerated report of a bloke down under
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the boastful phrase for a man said to be very well endowed

explanation.surface: A journalist hack facing suspension over a wildly overblown story about an Australian man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' and 'down under' suggest a reporter and Australia; a hack is also a horse, and 'down under' is the groin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a crude boast about genital size; read literally it describes a horse that has been strung up.

clue.text: Old poet's ejaculation when on speed

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other, so this cry comes first

parts.note: an exclamation; 'ho!' is a cry of surprise or attention
to race is to go at speed; race as a noun is a speed contest

explanation.surface: A crude joke about a classical poet's climax while high on amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ejaculation' in its old sense is just an exclamation, and 'speed' is not the drug but a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a Roman lyric poet of the first century BC, author of the Odes.

clue.text: Prescott? Shit!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John Prescott was Tony Blair's deputy prime minister, his second in command
second meaning: a childish euphemism for a poo

explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was the UK Deputy Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007, hence Blair's deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: The deputy to a leader is called their second in command, and the nursery phrase means excrement.

clue.text: Give up sex partner, getting depressed

parts.note: a lay is slang for a sexual partner
feeling down means feeling depressed

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a lover and sinks into gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender, as in putting down your arms, relinquishing them.

clue.text: Some mistake MP Tony for orderly

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A warning not to confuse a Member of Parliament called Tony with a tidy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and well groomed; the word survives mostly in its negative unkempt but is a real adjective for tidy.

clue.text: See 1
Blustering and removing board members

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... and puffing, blowing hard in indignation
second meaning: in draughts, ... is taking an opponent's piece as a penalty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Board members' looks like a company board; it is the pieces on a draughts board, where removing a piece that failed to capture is called huffing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: angry puffing, and the draughts rule of forfeiting a piece.

clue.text: Tory women stalwarts' crowning glory, if blue, lies in their insecurity

definitions.text: Tory women stalwarts' crowning glory, if blue

indicators.note: lies in says the answer is found sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dig at the vanity and anxiety of elderly Conservative women.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue rinse is a hair tint associated with elderly Conservative ladies, whose hair is their crowning glory.

clue.text: Swearing about American outpouring

indicators.note: about tells us the swearing word goes round the American letters

parts.note: effing is swearing, using the f-word

explanation.surface: An American's foul-mouthed rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusing means pouring forth, used as a participle like outpouring.

clue.text: Murdoch's business has fair pain, reportedly, at the top

definitions.note: pain sounds like pane, so this means a window pane in the roof

parts.note: Sky is the satellite broadcaster founded by Rupert Murdoch
fair hair is light hair

explanation.surface: Rupert Murdoch's company suffers a modest headache in its boardroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on sound: a pain at the top of the business is a pane at the top of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A window set into a roof is a pane of glass at the top of a building.

clue.text: Sex with topless dwarf having tendency to fart

indicators.note: topless says the first letter of the dwarf's name is removed

parts.note: Grumpy is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs
to pump is slang for breaking wind, so pumpy means given to it

explanation.surface: An unappetising sexual encounter with a flatulent little man.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming British phrase is a jocular term for sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Mock force (United Nations) off gallivanting about

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them

indicators.note: about tells us the rearranged letters go round the other piece
gallivanting means roaming about, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Ridiculing a UN peacekeeping force that goes off roaming.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule or tease someone is to poke fun, the phrasal verb meaning tease.

clue.text: Singer too pissed for a smoke

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A pop star who is too drunk wants a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pissed' here means drunk, as in British slang, and it rearranges TOO into OOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, something to smoke.

clue.text: Hangs around some opportunistic 'post-liberation' Iraqis when one replaces occupiers' leader

indicators.note: replaces says one letter is swapped in for another

parts.note: looters ransacked Baghdad after the 2003 invasion

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Satire on the looting that followed the 2003 'liberation' of Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: In LOOTERS, the O (first letter of 'occupiers'') is replaced by I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly, a verb with the same tense as the definition.

clue.text: Going down, clenching tip of tongue and humming

indicators.note: clenching means gripping tightly, so the sinking word holds the other letter

parts.note: a ship going down is sinking

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Suggests a sexual act involving the tongue and humming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humming' looks like a sound, but it is British slang for smelling bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is British slang for smelling strongly, like the adjective for a foul odour.

clue.text: "N.O.R.W.C.H" scrawled on top of missive — creepy little bugger!

indicators.note: scrawled means written messily, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the lovers' code N.O.R.W.I.C.H. written on the backs of envelopes

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A saucy lover's code written on a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints the acronym without its I, but NORWICH plus M (top of 'missive') is what rearranges into the answer. NORWICH, for 'knickers off ready when I come home', was written on wartime love letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inchworm is a looper caterpillar, a small crawling creature that moves by arching its body.

clue.text: Don't be an outsider guarding Blair's rear — and genital area

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding protectively, so the phrase holds the letter

parts.note: to go in is to enter rather than stay outside

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Tony Blair, the prime minister; the possessive just links him to his rear

explanation.surface: A crude jibe about getting close behind Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: The groin is the fold where the thigh meets the abdomen, the region of the private parts.

clue.text: Cooking unmanly? Oh, just what you'd expect from one of us

definitions.text: just what you'd expect from one of us

indicators.note: cooking means rustling up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a man cooking is unmanly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase excuses a failing as natural for any person, since we are all mortal and flawed.

clue.text: Devious scheme to accommodate long-suffering character

parts.note: to put someone up is to give them lodging
Job is the biblical figure famed for his patience in suffering

explanation.surface: A cunning plan to house a patient sufferer.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-up job is a fraud or set-up arranged in advance to deceive.

clue.text: About getting buggered: it used to be a danger 'below'

definitions.text: it used to be a danger 'below'

indicators.note: buggered is British slang for wrecked, so these letters are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A crude remark that seems to link sodomy and the call 'below' on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine of the world wars, a threat to shipping from beneath the waves.

clue.text: Goes through the motions as a lover?

definitions.text: Goes through the motions as a lover?

parts.words: Goes through the motions as a lover?
parts.note: going through the motions usually means acting half-heartedly; here it is the physical movements of sex

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for doing something mechanically is read literally as the movements of lovemaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelvic pushes during intercourse are the repeated movements a lover makes.

clue.text: They're produced by Hooters, Pussy & Tossers' predictions

parts.note: a pussy is a cat
when a coin is tossed, the call is a guess of heads or tails

explanation.surface: A smutty list that sounds like a seedy bar and its clientele.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooters is a US restaurant chain known for its waitresses; here hooters are simply people who hoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeers or shrill whistles of derision are the noises an audience of hooters makes.

clue.text: Stiff examination dashing past you

indicators.note: dashing means rushing about, so these letters race into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sprinting past you on the way to a tough exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like an adjective meaning difficult; it is a noun, slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem is a medical inspection of a dead body, a stiff in slang.

clue.text: Dolly's bust? It had a number of unfortunate names

definitions.text: It had a number of unfortunate names

indicators.note: bust means broken, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Dolly Parton's bosom and the unflattering nicknames it attracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Names' are Lloyd's of London's investors, many ruined by huge losses in the early 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: The London insurance market relies on wealthy backers called Names, many of whom suffered disastrous losses.

clue.text: Take apart Bush's far from favourite organisation's team

parts.note: George W Bush clashed with the United Nations over Iraq; UN's is its abbreviation with the possessive
a crew is a team of workers

explanation.surface: Dismantling a UN team that George W Bush disliked.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle by loosening screws, taking something to pieces.

clue.text: All right, the intelligence service's lost a flipping nutter

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: OK means all right

indicators.note: lost says the letter A drops out of the agency's name

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency; with the possessive S it gives CIAS

explanation.surface: The spy agency is fine, but it has mislaid a deranged person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost a' takes A from CIAS to leave CIS; OKCIS is then reversed by 'flipping'. 'Flipping' also passes for a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sicko is slang for a mentally disturbed or perverted person, a maniac.

clue.text: Old bag sees Southwark's premier gay rights activist get his wings clipped

indicators.note: the premier letter of a word is its first
clipping both wings removes the outer letters at each end

parts.note: Peter Tatchell is a British gay rights campaigner, once Labour candidate in Southwark

explanation.surface: Peter Tatchell, who stood in the 1983 Bermondsey by-election in Southwark, is cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Tatchell is a British gay rights activist; losing his 'wings' (first and last letters) leaves ATCHEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, traditionally an old-fashioned school bag.

clue.text: Cop booze on Brenda

indicators.note: in a down clue the drinking word sits on top of the Queen

parts.note: to sup is to drink
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: A policeman getting the Queen drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda'; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A super is short for a superintendent, a senior police rank.

clue.text: Male athlete's trick for keeping equipment safely in place

definitions.text: for keeping equipment safely in place
definitions.note: a thing for holding the male genitals in place; 'equipment' is slang for them

parts.note: a jock is a sporty male athlete; the possessive gives JOCKS
a trap is a trick to catch someone

explanation.surface: A sportsman's method for securing his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equipment' sounds like sports kit, but it is slang for the genitals the garment holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockstrap is an athletic support garment that holds the male genitals during sport.

clue.text: See 10
Dishevelled but gives head boy no personal problem

parts.note: blows is slang for performing oral sex

indicators.note: no says the problem letters are taken out of the word boy

parts.note: BO is body odour, a personal hygiene problem

explanation.surface: A scruffy man insists oral sex with a boy is no problem for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowsy describes someone untidy and coarse-looking, especially a red-faced slovenly woman.

clue.text: Mini 'Ground Force' trashy series starts after many a right bust-up

indicators.note: after places those initial letters behind the rearranged ones
a bust-up is a fight that smashes things, so the letters are broken and rearranged
starts takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Mocking the BBC garden-makeover show Ground Force as trash after a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground Force was a BBC TV garden makeover show; read literally it is a force on the ground. 'bust-up' rearranges MANY A R into ARMYAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Army ants are tiny insects that march in huge columns, literally a small military force on the ground.
